Nobody ships 8 billion rows to a browser, so the GPU simulates them. A compute shader gives every person a deterministic random draw and casts their 8 ballots, then adds the votes into a data cube of place × age × proposal × vote, about 49 MB on the GPU. That is the imMens idea: brushing queries the cube, never the raw rows.

Population comes from real city populations (GeoNames) and approximate national totals, scaled to exactly 8 billion on a half-degree grid. Votes are invented. Support depends on the voter's age, how urban the cell is, the country's age profile, and smooth random regional variation, so the map reflects no real polling. Everyone gets a ballot, children included; brush the age chart to 18+ for adults only.
